- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5% above peak or use 3-period moving average for smoothing.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00), model overconfidently holds high forecasts; apply downward bias of 2–5% for 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 3–5 day horizon: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, adjust down by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often ignores sentiment decay; if sentiment drops below 0.33 after 5 days, reduce forecast slope by 50% for next 3 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 0.33, 0.67), model overfits to recent highs; use 10-day rolling average to dampen volatility.
